name: Greater Adjutant
rangeDescription: Formerly from northern india to vietnam, dispersing west to pakistan; currently breeds northeastern india (assam) and cambodia, with dispersal west to nepal
description: Immense and imposing undertaker of a stork with a bare head and neck, pale eyes, and dark gray wings. Overlaps in some areas with similar but smaller Lesser Adjutant; note pale wing panel, paler heavier bill, prominent white neck ruff, and when in flight, grayer and less contrasting underwing.

name: Serra do Mar Bristle-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Coastal mountains of southeastern brazil (espírito santo to northern rio grande do sul)
description: Tiny flycatcher with a long slender tail. Differs from other tyrannulets in being mostly bright olive-green above and gray below with darkish ear patches, prominent white eyerings, and pinkish (not dark) legs.

name: Mountain Owlet-nightjar
rangeDescription: Mountains of new guinea, from the bird's head peninsula, the wandammen mountains, and the foja mountains, through central new guinea to the huon and southeastern peninsulas
description: A small owlet-nightjar of montane forests. Dark head, pale collar, barred back and tail.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Javan Fulvetta
rangeDescription: Forest of western and central java
description: Unremarkable-looking warm brown songbird. Endemic to Java’s montane and submontane broadleaf forests, where it is a common member of mixed flocks.

name: Monotonous Lark
rangeDescription: Southwestern angola to southern zambia, northern namibia, zimbabwe, and northern cape province
description: A medium-small, compact lark with a small bill, a plain face, and an indistinct eyebrow. It has streaky upperparts with a distinct rufous wing panel and a lightly-streaked buffy chest that separates the white throat from the pale belly.

name: Hispaniolan Crossbill
rangeDescription: Cordillera central of dominican republic and adjacent haiti
description: A gregarious species of montane pine forests. This species can be deceptively hard to find when not calling, despite its bright colors and tendency to travel in flocks of up to twenty.

name: Sri Lanka Drongo
rangeDescription: Western sri lanka
description: Large, upright, blackish bird with a long, deeply-forked tail and tuft of feathers on the forehead. Typically found in pairs, often in mixed flocks, within the understory of humid forests in the lowlands and foothills of Sri Lanka’s Wet Zone.

name: Tawny-collared Nightjar
rangeDescription: Tropical eastern mexico (nuevo león to oaxaca and chiapas)
description: Fairly large dark nightjar of woodland, edge, and adjacent clearings in northeast Mexico. Hunts mainly from perches at forest edge, sometimes even on fence posts in rather open areas.

name: Lemon-spectacled Tanager
rangeDescription: Tropical eastern panama (darién) to western colombia and northwestern ecuador
description: Chunky tanager, unlikely to be mistaken within limited range from eastern Panama to extreme northwest Ecuador. Mostly dull olive with brighter yellow throat and bold yellow spectacles.

name: Pink-legged Graveteiro
rangeDescription: Southeastern bahia and extreme northeastern minas gerais, eastern brazil
description: Predominantly gray species with a long tail and pink legs. Note the darker gray crown and paler eyebrow.

name: Turquoise-winged Parrotlet
rangeDescription: Northern colombia
description: Tiny parrot with green body, short pointed tail, and pale bill. Males have blue wings and cerulean rump; females are all green.

name: Emerald-spotted Wood-Dove
rangeDescription: Woodland and thornscrub of east and southern africa
description: A small, dainty, pinkish-fawn, ground-dwelling dove with an all-dark bill and two rows of iridescent green spots on the wing. In flight it reveals bright rufous wings and three gray bands: two across the back and one across the tail.

name: Javan Hawk-Eagle
rangeDescription: Wooded hills of western java
description: Medium-sized eagle with short, rounded wings. Adult is dark brown above and white with heavy streaking and barring below.

name: Tepui Vireo
rangeDescription: Tepuis of southern venezuela, western guyana, and far northern brazil
description: Small, arboreal bird of tepui highlands. Olive-gray above and yellowish below, with a gray head, pinkish bill, and pale eye.

name: Blue Eared-Pheasant
rangeDescription: Montane forest of north-central china
description: A large gray terrestrial bird with an elegantly frilly tail. Bright red face and upswept white facial plumes (“ears”) are unique in its range.

name: Bismarck Woodswallow
rangeDescription: New ireland and new britain (eastern bismarck archipelago)
description: A thick-bodied, highly aerobatic bird, white-bodied above and below with black wings, a black hood, and an obvious pale eye-ring. Bill pale bluish with a limited dark tip.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Australian Crake
rangeDescription: Moist areas of southeastern and southwestern australia including tasmania
description: Very small, stocky rail with yellow legs and bill. Brown above, blue-gray below black streaking and white specks, barred flanks, and black undertail with a thick white border (unlike Baillon’s Crake, which has fine barring).

name: Halmahera Golden-Bulbul
rangeDescription: Northern moluccas (morotai, halmahera, bacan, and kasiruta)
description: A thrush-sized bird with a fairly long horn-colored bill. Uniform rich olive-green above and all yellow underneath, with dark eyes.

name: Madagascar Pochard
rangeDescription: Lac alaotra and lac matsaborimena (north-central and northwestern madagascar, respectively); thought extinct until rediscovered at lac matsaborimena in 2006
description: Extremely rare diving duck that was long thought extinct before being rediscovered in 2006 in a remote site in northern Madagascar. A large duck that is mostly rich brown, with white under the tail.

name: Hawaii Akepa
rangeDescription: Montane ohia and koa forest of hawaii
description: A small, rare Hawaiian honeycreeper of native forests above 5,000 feet elevation on Hawaii Island. Brilliant orange color of males is unique.
